issues.legal_issue: A guardian’s compromise withdrawing an application to set aside an execution sale does not require court leave when it does not affect rights or liabilities declared by the decree.
material_facts: A minor judgment-debtor was represented by a guardian in proceedings to execute a decree.

The guardian agreed with the decree-holder and auction purchaser to withdraw the application challenging the sale, give up the challenge to the sale’s validity, and deliver possession; the other parties gave up their claim for costs of the application.
The compromise left the rights and liabilities declared by the decree unchanged.
issues.conclusion: The compromise did not require court leave and was binding on the minor; the order dismissing the application could not be set aside on the ground that leave had not been obtained.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XXXII, rule 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure, an agreement or compromise with reference to a suit requires court leave when it concerns rights put in issue, rather than merely procedural steps. The rule applies during the suit and its execution proceedings, and the agreement must be with a party to the suit or proceeding. A judgment-debtor’s application to set aside an execution sale is a proceeding in execution, but a compromise in that proceeding requires leave only if it affects rights or liabilities declared by the decree. The court relied on Virupakshappa v. Shidappa and Basappa, Arunachellam Chetty v. Ramanadhan Chetty, Muthalakkammal v. Narappa Reddiar, Jitendra Nath Roy v. Samarendra Nath Mitter, and Katneni Venkatakrishnayya v. Garapati China Kanakayya.

rule.if: minor_party and guardian_represented_minor and execution_proceeding and application_challenged_execution_sale and compromise_with_party and decree_declared_rights_unchanged

predicates.minor_party: A minor was a party to the legal proceeding.
predicates.guardian_represented_minor: A guardian represented the minor in the proceeding.
predicates.execution_proceeding: The proceeding was part of the execution of a decree.
predicates.application_challenged_execution_sale: The application sought to set aside a sale conducted in execution of the decree.
predicates.compromise_with_party: The guardian made the compromise with a party to the suit or execution proceeding.
predicates.decree_declared_rights_unchanged: The compromise did not alter rights or liabilities declared by the decree.

issues.definition: When a guardian represents a minor in a proceeding to execute a decree and compromises with a party over an application challenging an execution sale without changing rights or liabilities declared by the decree, the compromise is binding on the minor.

issues.legal_issue: The general procedure for civil proceedings does not extend suit procedure to an application made in execution of a decree.
material_facts: The application to set aside the sale was made by a judgment-debtor in execution of a decree.
The application was a proceeding in execution, not an original proceeding in the nature of a suit.
issues.conclusion: Section 141 did not apply to the execution application and could not be used to extend Order XXXII, rule 7 to the compromise.
issues.legal_principle: Section 141 of the Code of Civil Procedure applies to original proceedings in the nature of suits, not proceedings in execution. The court relied on Thakur Prasad v. Sheikh Fakir Ullah and applied the established distinction between original proceedings and execution proceedings.

predicates.execution_proceeding: The proceeding was part of the execution of a decree.
predicates.application_to_set_aside_execution_sale: A judgment-debtor applied to set aside a sale conducted in execution of the decree.

issues.definition: When a judgment-debtor applies to set aside a sale in execution of a decree, suit procedure is not extended to that execution proceeding.
